title: Over-session names are not matched to the family being reported
description: `over_sessions` discards each volume check’s family, and `_family_evidence` aggregates names by product across coverage results. `over_failures` then uses that combined list for each family with an `over` count. The failure can therefore name sessions from a different family—or include duplicates—rather than identifying the sessions behind that family’s count. Keep the family with each name and filter names when constructing each failure.

title: Record totals silently omit families missing from the after snapshot
description: `totals_delta` detects families present after but absent before, but not families present before and missing after. Because it iterates only `after`, a family omitted from the accounting output disappears from the reported delta instead of stopping the cutover. Validate that the before and after family-key sets match before calculating deltas.

title: Estimate mode prices the installed release instead of the requested release
description: `preflight(ref)` checks that the ref exists but does not install it. `fetch_estimate()` invokes `mt-run`, which executes `/opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/mt`. When production still runs the previous release, `--estimate` prices the old universe, potentially reporting nothing to buy instead of the expanded history purchase. Run the estimate using the requested release’s configuration and add a regression test with different installed and requested universes.

title: Pre-install baseline lacks the newly added GC bar family
description: The baseline is captured before `install_release()`, using installed production accounting. The previous universe has no GC bar want, so its accounting omits `GC/bar_1m`. After installation and purchase, `purchase_accounting.totals_delta()` rejects that new family because its baseline is absent. Reruns retain the incomplete baseline and fail again. Capture verified pre-purchase totals for every target-release family and test this upgrade transition.

title: Per-session verification excludes the tick-tier families
description: `coverage_reads()` traverses only history wants, excluding ES and GC `tbbo`. Although accounting narrates those families, `_family_evidence()` never checks their sessions for unaccounted statuses or ledger mismatches. Consequently, an unchanged health exit code can allow success without satisfying D6’s every-family evidence requirement. Include each configured tier over its wanted range and test an unaccounted `tbbo` session.

title: Do not treat every provider hole as an accounted-for session
description: `not_caught_up_report` skips every `provider_hole` via `_LISTED_NEVER`, without checking the session’s `condition`. The exit criterion excludes only a provider hole on a missing day. A hole on another condition can therefore be omitted from the report and avoid an exit failure, allowing the cutover to pass with an unaccounted-for session. Only skip a provider hole when the coverage row confirms the missing-day condition; otherwise report and judge it.

title: Include unheld jobs when deriving the 30-day ceiling
description: `ceiling_values` derives the 30-day ceiling from `planned + trailing`, but the spend guard also counts unheld provider jobs toward that cap. The estimate summary exposes those jobs in `unheld_jobs`; when any are present, the printed command can still leave the guard refusing the purchase. Include their costs when deriving the suggested cap.

title: Collect the health rows required by the evidence step
description: The evidence collection reads and narrates accounting rows, but it does not collect the current health rows. `health_exit_code()` runs `mt data health` and returns only its exit code; that result is used for the baseline comparison, not included in the evidence. This leaves the required per-product health evidence absent from the narration.

title: Attribute over-session names to the matching family
description: `over_sessions` drops the volume check’s `family`, and `_family_evidence` groups the resulting names only by product. `over_failures` then uses that combined list for each family row with an `over` count. When multiple volume families have over sessions, a row can name sessions belonging to another family, making the evidence attribution incorrect. Preserve and filter by family when collecting and reporting those names.

title: The derived 30-day ceiling omits unheld provider spend and double-counts re-submits
description: `ceiling_values` (scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:88-91), `ceiling_command` (94-97) and the cap check in `judge_estimate` (line 244, `planned + trailing > cap_30d`) all work from `planned + trailing`. The guard that will actually authorise the purchase computes the breach differently: `evaluate_spend` in src/manta_trading/data/tick/spend_guard.py sums `trailing_total + unheld_total + planned_new`, where `unheld_total` is the cost of provider jobs no manifest row holds (the estimate itself reports these as `unheld_jobs`) and `planned_new` deliberately excludes re-submits whose cost is already inside `trailing`. Two consequences: (a) the command the PM is told to run can set a `--cap-30d` below what the guard demands, so the purchase it enables is still refused by `mt data tick pass`; (b) the cutover's own check is looser than the guard when unheld jobs exist and stricter than the guard for a re-submit (that cost is counted once in `planned` and again in `trailing`, while the guard counts it once). No test covers unheld jobs in the ceiling derivation (`test_ceiling_command_rounds_the_estimate_up_to_the_next_five` and `test_an_over_ceiling_estimate_carries_the_command_for_its_figures` only use `planned`/`trailing`).

title: The --estimate run never narrates the estimate's refusal reasons
description: `_estimate_only` prints `verdict {summary['verdict']}: {outcome}` (line 271) and then, whenever the outcome is `BUY`, the ceiling command (line 274) — but it never narrates `summary["reasons"]`, the list the planner fills with why the estimate was refused (absent or short ceilings, archive space short, provider costs). The full path does surface them: `judge_estimate` raises with `summary["reasons"]` (scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:249-252), so the estimate path loses exactly the information the operator needs to choose the ceilings. The output is also self-contradictory: with `check_ceilings=False`, `judge_estimate` returns `BUY` for every verdict other than `nothing_to_buy` (scripts/cutover_304_checks.py:232-233), so a plan refused for a non-ceiling reason still yields "verdict refused: buy", a ceiling command and exit code 0. No test asserts on the estimate's reasons.
